simple.meaning: גֵּלֶל (gêlel) is a Hebrew object word meaning “dung (plural balls of dung).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 20:7. The surrounding context includes blood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גֵּלֶל (H1561) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: גֵּלֶל (gêlel) / H1561 is traced through Job 20:7, Ezekiel 4:12, Ezekiel 4:15, Zephaniah 1:17 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H1561. gelel or gel [ גֵּל ] noun [masculine] dung ( ball of dung, Arabic etc., dung of camels etc., compare Aramaic גַּלָּא ; on form see Ew § 255 b Ol § 150. 163 ) — suffix גֶּלֲלוֺ Job 20:7 , plural construct הָאָדָם ( צֵאַת ) גֶּלֲלֵי Ezek 4:12 , 15 ; — human dung used as fuel 4:12 , 15 ׳ג הָאָדָם (צֵאַת) ; perhaps also Job 20:7 , but compare Di, who thinks no reference to fuel, & De who thinks of cattle-dung; (see on Arabic word Wetzst in De). — See also II. גָּלָל . גֻּלָּהּ גֹּל, see גֻּלָּה . below
